review.alternative: Passive degrees of freedom could theoretically increase dissipation if they mediate efficient energy coupling to a heat bath.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of increased dissipation in systems with added passive degrees of freedom under identical driving.

claims.statement: Non-driven, passive degrees of freedom generally lead to decreased dissipation in driven particle systems.

support.explanation: Provides a direct link between passive environmental components and reduced dissipation in driven systems.
support.passage: We use this finding to argue that the presence of non-driven, passive degrees of freedom generally leads to decreased dissipation.

review.alternative: Non-reciprocity could primarily facilitate heat transfer rather than information flow optimization.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing no correlation between non-reciprocal coupling strength and information flow throughput.

claims.statement: Non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines allow significant modulation of inter-dot information flow, enhancing energy conversion efficiency.

support.explanation: Non-reciprocity is identified as a mechanism for controlling information flow, which is central to optimizing energy conversion.
support.passage: we develop a thermodynamic framework that allows us to demonstrate that nonreciprocity can significantly modulate the inter-dot information flow, thereby providing a robust control mechanism.

review.alternative: Full entropy production might be reconstructible via specific inference algorithms without requiring full resolution.
review.would_change_mind: Publication of a robust, general-purpose method for retrieving exact entropy production from coarse-grained data.

claims.statement: Coarse-graining of underlying Markovian dynamics restricts the retrieval of entropy production to lower bounds.

support.explanation: Establishes a fundamental limit on measuring entropy production when system resolution is constrained.
support.passage: such an often inevitable coarse-graining implies that, rather than the full entropy production, only a lower bound can be retrieved from coarse-grained data.

actions.findings:
Non-driven, passive degrees of freedom generally lead to decreased dissipation in driven particle systems. [peer-30b9153ce0fe31018c8e3730]

Non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines allow significant modulation of inter-dot information flow, enhancing energy conversion efficiency. [peer-f3ee30889b8396e02ea0588a]

Coarse-graining of underlying Markovian dynamics restricts the retrieval of entropy production to lower bounds. [peer-42ea5272a464585193f493cc]
actions.limitations: Findings remain theoretical, primarily derived from Langevin and quantum-dot models; experimental validation of coarse-graining bounds in complex, non-Markovian environments remains an open challenge.
actions.next_questions: What are the specific quantitative limits of coarse-grained entropy bounds in systems with high-dimensional state spaces where non-Markovian effects dominate?
actions.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate new evidence on coarse-graining and thermodynamic costs of information erasure.
actions.summary: We synthesize findings on entropy production bounds and non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines, establishing that passive degrees of freedom and predictive information provide robust upper bounds on dissipation in driven physical systems.
actions.title: Predictive Dissipation and Information Engines (Revised)

proposal.summary: Institutional entry detailing the revision of predictive dissipation models and entropy production bounds in driven information engines.
proposal.title: WAKE✳︎ Research Journal Entry: Predictive Dissipation Dynamics
